response.markdown_report:
At 10% progress, select **gated text–ID fusion inside the corrected GRU4Rec** as the first experiment. Benefits remain hypotheses; no experiment was executed. Retain contextual text encoding, alignment and alternative objectives as subsequent separate trials.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Training separation is already strong. Electronics nevertheless has 4.56% wrong-order comparisons and 7.24% margins below 0.5, making residual confusion a diagnostic target rather than evidence of its cause. (2) Users reject conditionally relevant product matches and overly broad entertainment matches. Text may improve item distinctions, but token means cannot distinguish identical token multisets or reliably resolve prerequisites, negation and specification binding. (3) Concentration scores near 0.5 provide no evidence of broad directional collapse. They neither justify a collapse penalty nor measure recommendation diversity.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Ask the GRU](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02116) supports collaborative text learning, but both compared encoders use pretrained CBOW initialization. Its contextual GRU outperforms raw pooling in that setting; it establishes neither scratch-training success nor targeted negation understanding. (2) [ASIF](https://doi.org/10.1145/3589335.3648308) motivates controlling side-information noise; alignment remains a separate intervention. (3) [DenseRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18442) motivates content projection, but its pretrained setting differs. (4) [Modality controls](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07399) motivate capacity and shuffled-content comparisons; [Amazon multimodal evidence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.12911) motivates checking popularity shortcuts.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Intervention | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Representation | Shared text–ID item vectors | Specificity versus lexical shortcuts |
| Supervision | Same-item alignment | Transfer versus representation distortion |
| Optimization | BPR-max | Hard discrimination versus false negatives |
| Semantic capacity | Small contextual text encoder | Order sensitivity versus supervision and compute cost |

Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment gives a positive and a limitation for every dimension in that order.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gated text fusion | 2/6/6/5/5 | Focused adaptation; reusable test; item distinctions; possible error reduction; small encoder | Established components; sparse supervision; lexical ambiguity; indirect diagnostic target; interface and caching work |
| Fusion plus duplicate-masked alignment | 3/6/6/5/6 | Explicit consistency; transfer research; item identity; regularization; standard loss | Established alignment; false negatives; specificity unproven; diagnostic gains uncertain; extra tuning |
| BPR-max alone | 2/6/4/8/4 | Family precedent; useful control; stronger competitors; direct separation objective; compact change | Established loss; false negatives; missing semantics; sampled errors differ from HR; sampling integration |
| Contextual text fusion | 3/7/7/5/6 | Order-sensitive adaptation; binding research; richer distinctions; possible separation; small text GRU | Established encoders; scratch data limits; comprehension unproven; indirect target; extra compute |

**Chosen algorithm.** Train token means and a bias-free text projection jointly with GRU4Rec. Add a scalar-gated text residual to each item ID, conditioned on training frequency and text availability; initialize slope to zero and bias to −3. Share fused vectors between history and candidate scoring; preserve the baseline loss, sampler and optimizer.

This targets **conditionally relevant product matches**, **overly broad entertainment matches**, and **Electronics’ sampled ranking errors**. These are eligible but unverified mechanisms; mean pooling cannot establish compatibility, ownership needs or current intent. First compare ID-only and fusion. Subsequently test fixed gates, capacity controls, frequency-bin text shuffling and contextual encoding separately. Select by pinned macro validation HR@10. Track residual/ID norms, branch alignment and frequency strata; gate size alone is not identifiable evidence of content usefulness. Preserve four routes, one checkpoint/category, fixed seeds/splits, padding, diagnostic interfaces and predictor parity.

idea.description: Add a scratch-trained token-pooling title/description encoder to the supplied corrected GRU4Rec. Fuse its projected output with each item-ID embedding through a frequency-conditioned scalar gate, using the identical fused representation in observed-history encoding and candidate scoring. Train and deploy one jointly trained network per category. Keep this minimal representation intervention first; contextual text encoding, alignment, BPR-max and temporal-memory changes remain separate alternative trials.
idea.motivation: The intervention explicitly targets two supplied user-facing failures: conditionally relevant products promoted through broad associations, and entertainment recommendations that overgeneralize specific preferences into broad genres or formats. Item-specific words may improve distinctions, but raw token means necessarily map identical token multisets to the same text representation; the method cannot claim negation-scope, prerequisite or numeric attribute-binding understanding. ID embeddings may still distinguish such items, which would not demonstrate textual understanding. The model-facing target is Electronics’ measured 4.56% sampled wrong-order rate and 7.24% small-margin rate, followed by Industrial_and_Scientific’s 3.42% wrong-order rate. These training diagnostics establish neither the cause of validation errors nor expected gains. Current concentration scores provide no evidence requiring an embedding-collapse penalty. At 10% progress, the small representation intervention remains preferable to simultaneously changing objective, sampling and recurrence, provided its semantic limitations and integration costs are explicit.
idea.implementation_notes:
The supplied baseline source is absent from the prompt, so this is an integration specification rather than an executable replacement train.py. No training, diagnostics or validation were performed. Preserve the supplied baseline’s resolved GRU dimensions, recurrent layers, projections, dropout, objective, sampler, optimizer, batch size, gradient clipping, regularization and checkpoint-selection schedule for the first experiment. Record their actual values and software versions in the trial configuration; do not substitute guessed defaults. Retain the GRU backbone and corrected padding-state handling. Exact end-to-end reproduction requires the host baseline and its resolved configuration in addition to this report.

Use only public item titles/descriptions and training histories. Fit the vocabulary using documents belonging to items observed in training, never validation/test interaction labels. Initial proposed settings are vocabulary cap 30,000 including reserved tokens, minimum token frequency 2, token dimension 64, and at most 32 title plus 96 description tokens. Specify the tokenizer reproducibly: Unicode NFKC normalization, lowercase, regex tokenization with pattern \w+|[^\w\s], tokens counted before per-document truncation, descending-frequency vocabulary order with lexical tie-breaking, PAD index 0 and UNK index 1. Join the separately truncated title and description token lists; record the exact regex library/version. Read only title/description fields, treating missing fields as empty strings and joining list-valued descriptions in source order. Persist the resulting vocabulary and per-item token buffers, so prediction does not depend on retokenization. These are proposed settings, not measured optima. Missing or token-empty text receives an exactly zero residual; an all-UNK nonempty document remains available and its occurrence rate should be reported. Items outside the fitted vocabulary use UNK without refitting. Do not expand the supplied item universe or routing.

Cache token IDs and masks during training, never detached learned item representations. Token embeddings and projection must receive recommendation gradients. Obtain item counts from training interactions only, never validation/test targets. Let z_i be standardized log1p(training_count_i), with mean and population standard deviation computed across real items having positive training count. Serialize both statistics, use a denominator clamped to at least 1e-8, and apply the same transform to zero-count real items without recomputing statistics. Availability is determined by the token mask, independent of frequency.

Define text_i = bias_free_projection(masked_mean(token_embedding(tokens_i))). Define gate_i = available_i * sigmoid(a * z_i + b), initializing a=0 and b=-3. Define fused_i = id_embedding_i + gate_i * text_i; item zero must remain exactly zero regardless of branch parameters. Initialize the added token embeddings with the baseline ID embedding’s initialization rule and scale, and use PyTorch’s default bias-free Linear initialization for the projection; record both resolved rules. Preserve the baseline initialization and RNG sequence for its original modules before initializing added modules. This starts with a small nonzero gate, not necessarily a small residual norm and not baseline equivalence. Keep baseline branch scaling and scoring behavior otherwise unchanged. Do not introduce alignment losses, semantic negative filtering, popularity scores, recency branches, temporal gates or extra encoder dropout in the first trial. Preserve baseline occurrence-level dropout at its original locations.

The gate is an adaptive parameterization, not an identifiable attribution of content usefulness. Projection and token-embedding norms can compensate for gate changes, and unrestricted item-ID vectors can absorb additive text changes. The frequency-dependent sigmoid does not imply arbitrary exact rescaling across all items, but gate means alone still cannot show that the model uses reliable text or protects rare items. Measure actual residual magnitude and validation behavior instead of interpreting the gate as confidence or intent.

Make representations accessible consistently: retain item_emb through an embedding-compatible module whose forward returns fused vectors and whose weight access, if required by ModelView, returns the current fused table without detaching gradients. Preserve required attributes such as num_embeddings, embedding_dim and padding_idx, and audit uses of embedding-specific methods or regularizers rather than assuming attribute compatibility is sufficient. Distinguish original ID-weight regularization from penalties on fused vectors; do not silently replace one with the other. Preserve log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and all supported candidate-shape semantics. Both history encoding and candidate scoring must call the same fused embedding implementation. Diagnostic item sampling must use actual fused vectors while view.model remains the actual trained module.

Avoid full differentiable table construction for sampled training. Where the baseline call structure permits, concatenate requested history/positive/negative IDs, obtain unique_ids and inverse with torch.unique(..., return_inverse=True), encode each unique item once, then reconstruct original occurrences with encoded[inverse] and restore their original shapes. Preserve occurrence multiplicity, masks and the original loss denominator; never average the loss over unique IDs or detach reconstructed vectors. Deduplication preserves deterministic encoder gradients only under the relevant embedding semantics. Inspect scale_grad_by_freq and max_norm: the former changes behavior when lookup frequencies change, while the latter mutates weights during forward. If the baseline uses either and equivalence is not established, retain occurrence-level encoding rather than silently changing semantics. Keep original full-table regularization full-table and occurrence-weighted penalties occurrence-weighted. AdamW decay is not interchangeable with either. If encoder dropout is explored later, deduplication shares its mask across occurrences; apply intended occurrence-level dropout after reconstruction and treat any changed stochastic semantics as a separate intervention.

The corrected GRU must skip padding updates or use its established equivalent implementation; zero input alone does not prevent recurrent bias updates. Zero padding features after biased projections. Inference gathers the maximum index where sequence != 0, never count-1, and retains explicit baseline empty-history behavior. No shifted positive target may enter the observed-history encoder. Preserve the original causal training alignment and all valid-position masks.

Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Honor the host SASREC_EPOCHS setting within that maximum; the host default is 200. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Use one GPU per trial and account for training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Do not inspect other trials, reuse their checkpoints, read hidden tests, fetch extra datasets or use pretrained weights. The task-specific availability restriction overrides generic metadata examples: reviews, ratings, prices, stores, item-category attributes and simulator diversity/conformity traits are unavailable.

Save one selected checkpoint per category containing the complete jointly trained network, vocabulary, token IDs/masks, training counts/statistics and resolved configuration. Update the embedded predictor writer with the identical model definition, buffers, state-dict keys and scoring path. Verify fresh predictor loading against the selected in-memory model on identical left-padded inputs and candidate IDs, including multiple padding lengths and empty histories. Use the supplied ID-only baseline comparison and this fusion intervention first. This contrast estimates the total representation/parameterization change, not semantic transfer alone. If budget remains, separately retrain controls in a declared order: fixed gate sigmoid(-3), item-text shuffling within training-frequency bins, an active parameter-matched ID-only capacity control, then a small contextual text encoder. Keep each as one independent GRU4Rec network per category; never fuse their predictions. A capacity control must specify its active architecture and verify parameter counts before running; unused padding parameters do not constitute matching. For fixed-gate comparisons preserve encoder and all non-gate settings, noting the tiny parameter-count difference.

Define frequency bins before examining outcomes: sort positive-count training items by (count, item_id), partition into three bins of near-equal item count, and serialize boundaries/assignments. Use a separate analysis/control RNG seed 42 for a within-bin permutation of complete token/mask documents, without changing training RNG. This preserves the document collection and approximately preserves frequency structure while disrupting item alignment; it does not exactly match document-length or availability distributions at every frequency and does not eliminate all confounding. Keep count-conditioned gates tied to original item counts. Log permutation fixed points and do not tune permutations on validation. Retraining with shuffled text tests the training intervention; inference-only shuffling or branch removal measures reliance under distribution shift and is not equivalent evidence.

A later contextual text trial can replace token means with a small scratch-trained unidirectional text GRU followed by masked mean pooling over contextual states; the recommendation backbone remains GRU4Rec. Reuse vocabulary, truncation, baseline recommendation training and available controls, and disclose additional parameters/compute. Order sensitivity alone does not prove semantic understanding. Controlled same-token-multiset reorderings can establish that raw pooling is invariant, but negation-scope or numeric-binding accuracy requires authentic, auditable examples and appropriate labels. Do not fabricate such evaluation labels or substitute synthetic perturbation outcomes for benchmark HR@10. SWEM and Ask the GRU motivate comparisons without resolving this exact scratch-only recommendation setting.

Select only using pinned equal-weight macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42 and the existing checkpoint schedule. Log every attempted setting and per-category results. Frequency-stratified validation analysis is optional only when the host exposes target IDs/outcomes; report counts and do not manufacture unavailable observations. One changed hit alters category HR by 0.005 and macro HR by 0.00125. If paired per-user outcomes are available, an analysis-only seed-42 paired bootstrap can resample users within category and average the four category differences per replicate; respect shared-user clusters if present. Such intervals condition on fitted models and fixed candidates and do not correct adaptive model/checkpoint selection or cover training-seed uncertainty. Keep the search small and retain all attempts to limit optimistic interpretation. Neither increased margins, gate values, qualitative simulator judgments nor sampled HR gains establish compatibility, redundancy reduction or full-catalog utility; untouched final evaluation remains the host’s responsibility.
idea.pseudocode:
class FusedItemEmbedding(nn.Module):
    # Dimensions and original initialization come from corrected GRU4Rec.
    # Token buffers, count statistics, and vocabulary are checkpointed.
    def encode(self, item_ids):
        ids = self.id_embedding(item_ids)
        tokens = self.item_tokens[item_ids]
        mask = self.item_token_mask[item_ids]
        words = self.token_embedding(tokens)
        pooled = (words * mask[..., None]).sum(-2)
        pooled = pooled / mask.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1)
        text = self.text_projection(pooled)  # bias=False
        available = mask.any(-1, keepdim=True).to(text.dtype)
        frequency = self.standardized_log_count[item_ids][..., None]
        gate = available * sigmoid(self.gate_slope * frequency + self.gate_bias)
        fused = ids + gate * text
        return fused * (item_ids != 0)[..., None]

    def forward(self, item_ids):
        return self.encode(item_ids)

# Initialize gate_slope=0 and gate_bias=-3.
# Use the same module in history encoding and candidate scoring.
# Preserve the baseline objective, sampler, dropout, and regularization semantics.

def optionally_encode_requested_occurrences(flat_ids):
    if deduplication_semantics_verified:
        unique_ids, inverse = torch.unique(flat_ids, return_inverse=True)
        return model.item_emb(unique_ids)[inverse]  # keep gradients and multiplicity
    return model.item_emb(flat_ids)

DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
for category in FOUR_SUPPLIED_CATEGORIES:
    set_training_seed(42)
    train_data = supplied_training_split_preprocessed_with_seed_0(category)
    vocabulary, token_buffers = encode_public_training_item_documents(
        train_data, normalization='NFKC', lowercase=True,
        vocabulary_cap=30000, min_frequency=2,
        title_limit=32, description_limit=96)
    counts, count_statistics = training_only_item_counts(train_data)
    model = corrected_GRU4Rec_with_fused_item_embedding(
        resolved_baseline_config, vocabulary, token_buffers, counts, count_statistics)
    verify_bounded_padding_encoding_and_gradient_checks()
    for epoch in range(min(resolved_host_epochs, 200)):
        model.train()
        invalidate_inference_item_cache()
        for step in range(200):
            batch = unchanged_family_sample_batch()
            loss = unchanged_baseline_objective(model, batch)
            unchanged_optimizer_step(loss)
        unchanged_host_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_all_encoding_state(category)
write_predictor_with_identical_model_and_four_category_routing()
verify_loaded_predictor_score_parity()

def prediction(sequence, candidates):
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    positions = arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = where(sequence != 0, positions[None, :], -1).amax(dim=1)
    # Handle last == -1 using corrected baseline behavior before gathering.
    return score_final_valid_features_or_handle_empty(model, features, last, candidates)

# Optional item-dependent inference cache: never use it during training.
model.load_state_dict(selected_checkpoint)
model.eval()
with torch.inference_mode():
    item_cache = encode_real_items_in_bounded_chunks(model.item_emb)
    verify_cached_and_direct_scores_agree()
    # For native full-catalog recommendations, stream candidate score chunks,
    # apply original unseen-item/padding masks, and maintain global top-k.

# DiagnosisProbe and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt retain required signatures.
# Compute margins through actual fused features and candidate scoring.
# Report gate, residual/ID norm ratio, branch cosine, support, and definitions.
# Gate size and norm ratio are descriptive, not causal attribution.
# Fixed-gate, shuffled-text, capacity, contextual-encoder, and loss alternatives
# are separately trained trials; deploy exactly one checkpoint per category.
# No experiments or gains are asserted here.

originality.positive: The frequency-conditioned residual defines a focused, attributable adaptation within one GRU4Rec, with shared history/candidate representations and explicit semantic-noise controls.
originality.negative: Joint text–collaborative learning, content projection, pooling and gated fusion are established. The contribution is an experimental adaptation; the supplied references do not establish an exact prior-art boundary or a novel semantic capability.

future_potential.positive: A small representation intervention can establish whether training-supervised text helps this constrained setting and motivate controlled work on sparse-item transfer, contextual encoding and semantic noise.
future_potential.negative: Scratch supervision may be insufficient, raw pooling loses order and binding information, and frequency-conditioned fusion may amplify popularity or lexical shortcuts. Sampled validation gains would not establish actionable full-catalog utility.

code_difficulty.positive: Masked token pooling and a scalar gate preserve fused recurrent execution and require no pretrained assets, additional predictor or changed recommendation objective.
code_difficulty.negative: Embedding-interface compatibility, gradient-preserving deduplication, regularization semantics, full-catalog caching, text-state serialization, diagnostic adaptation and exact predictor parity make integration moderately difficult despite the small encoder.

related_work.title: Ask the GRU: Multi-task Learning for Deep Text Recommendations
contributions: Provides precedent for learning text representations through collaborative recommendation and auxiliary metadata supervision.
Compares raw word-embedding means with stacked order-sensitive GRUs; contextual GRU states are themselves averaged.
The supplied search reports cold-start Recall@50 on CiteULike-a/t of 38.53/35.85 for Embed, 46.16/47.59 for GRU, 41.71/38.16 for Embed-MTL and 49.76/51.22 for GRU-MTL.
limitations: Both encoders initialize word embeddings with CBOW pretrained on 440,756 ACM abstracts, so these results do not establish scratch-only performance.
Does not implement the required sequential GRU4Rec architecture or this pinned Amazon evaluation.
Negation motivates the architecture but is not evaluated with a controlled negation benchmark; specifications and lexical shortcuts lack targeted ablations.

related_work.title: ASIF (2024)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes contrastive ID–side-information alignment and orthogonal decomposition for shared information.
limitations: Does not establish an HR@10 benefit for this scratch-trained GRU4Rec intervention.
Adding alignment immediately would confound the first representation-only experiment.

related_work.title: DenseRec (2025)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes projecting pretrained content embeddings into ID space and examining unseen-item sequence representations.
limitations: Its pretrained content setting differs from the required scratch-trained encoder.
Its reported mechanism cannot be assumed to hold on these fixed Amazon splits.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides cross-entropy and BPR-max objectives as relevant GRU-family optimization alternatives.
limitations: Changing objectives does not itself supply item-specific textual distinctions.
Loss and sampling changes should remain separate trials for attribution; preserve the supplied baseline objective for the first fusion experiment.

related_work.title: SWEM: Baseline Models for Text Classification and Matching
contributions: Provides adjacent evidence comparing simple word-embedding pooling with more complex text architectures.
limitations: Text classification and matching results do not establish recommendation performance.
Does not resolve scratch-only pooling versus contextual encoding with separate binding, negation, sparse-item and shortcut tests in this benchmark.

related_work.title: Are Multimodal Embeddings Truly Beneficial for Recommendation?
contributions: The supplied search describes constant/noise modality replacements that preserve architecture, motivating controls for capacity-confounded content ablations.
limitations: Does not establish the complete proposed GRU4Rec gate-control protocol or its expected gains.
Architecture-preserving controls alone do not establish semantic understanding.

related_work.title: Malitesta et al.: Multimodal recommendation study
contributions: The supplied search reports that individual modalities can amplify popularity bias on Amazon datasets, motivating training-frequency analyses.
limitations: Does not establish that this scratch text encoder or frequency gate will amplify or reduce popularity bias.
Frequency-stratified sampled accuracy alone does not measure exposure fairness or actionable utility.

related_work.title: Attention Is Not Only a Weight
contributions: Shows why scalar weights should be interpreted alongside transformed-vector norms, motivating residual-magnitude diagnostics.
limitations: The analogy does not prove an exact rescaling symmetry for a frequency-dependent sigmoid gate.
Neither weights nor norms alone establish causal usefulness of the text branch.

related_work.title: Improving the Identifiability of Neural Networks for Bayesian Inference
contributions: Provides conceptual background on compensating parameter scalings and neural-network identifiability.
limitations: Does not analyze this GRU4Rec text gate directly.
The additive ID/text decomposition introduces its own nonuniqueness; exact invariances must not be inferred from analogy.

related_work.title: PyTorch unique mapping
contributions: Documents return_inverse reconstruction for encoding unique requested item IDs once while restoring occurrence order.
limitations: Correct loss weighting, autograd connectivity, dropout placement and embedding-frequency semantics remain implementation responsibilities.

related_work.title: PyTorch embedding implementation
contributions: Documents embedding behavior relevant to padding, scale_grad_by_freq and max_norm.
limitations: Deduplicating lookups can change frequency-scaled gradients; max_norm can mutate weights during forward.
A fused embedding wrapper must preserve the host’s actual access and regularization contracts.

related_work.title: PyTorch AdamW
contributions: Defines decoupled weight decay, clarifying its distinction from explicit embedding penalties.
limitations: Does not justify replacing the baseline’s regularization or optimizer during the representation-only experiment.

related_work.title: PyTorch inference mode
contributions: Documents inference-mode execution and restrictions relevant to caching trained item representations.
limitations: Inference mode does not set evaluation mode; model.eval() is also required.
Inference tensors must not be reused in autograd training, and cache invalidation remains the implementation’s responsibility.
